author: Forbes
description:
Inside Michelin’s 3,300-Acre Testing Facility: The Ultimate Tire-Buying Blueprint

Tires represent one of the most critical—yet widely misunderstood—components of vehicle safety, performance, and efficiency. To unpack the science behind modern rubber engineering, host Scotty Reiss spent the day at Michelin’s premier Laurens Proving Grounds in Laurens, South Carolina. Spanning 3,300 acres and 12 specialized test tracks, this high-security facility serves as the primary research and development proving ground where Michelin collaborates directly with global automaker OEMs and motorsport teams to engineer vehicle-specific tire lines.

Guided by Michelin Senior Subjective Test Driver Derek Secord, the visit subjects four distinct vehicle classes to extreme, real-world track experiments:  

—The Cheap Tire Trap: Testing a Chrysler Pacifica on MICHELIN CrossClimate 2 all-weather rubber directly against a sport-tuned BMW 4 Series fitted with low-cost "tier 4" budget tires on a high-speed wet
title: Inside Michelin’s Secret Test Track: Why Most Drivers Buy The Wrong Tires
